title: Airline Notices Standing on a Booking (Air Ticket Fare Brands)
content:
**Air Ticket Fare Brands — what a carrier's notices standing on a booking confer.**

1. On a booking sold under Air Ticket Fare Brands that the traveller has given up, what the airline's notices standing on the booking add to the amount returned follows how many of them the booking received in the last six months, whether or not any one of them was large enough to give the traveller a right of its own.

2. Where two or more airline notices stand on the booking from the last six months, the repeat-notice goodwill of 60.00 US dollars is added to the amount returned.

3. Where exactly one airline notice stands on the booking from the last six months, the single-notice goodwill of 25.00 US dollars is added to the amount returned.

4. Otherwise nothing is added for airline notices.

5. The number counted is the number of airline notices posted on the booking within the last six months. On hypothetical figures: a booking carrying three such notices adds 60.00 to the amount returned, as does a booking carrying exactly two; a booking carrying exactly one adds 25.00 to the amount returned; a booking carrying none has nothing added for airline notices. A booking carrying one notice posted within the last six months and two notices posted earlier than six months back adds 25.00 to the amount returned, the older notices standing outside the window that is counted.

6. The size of a notice and what it entitled the traveller to at the time do not enter this term; only the number standing on the booking from the last six months does.
